key_insight: The paper introduces a learned iterative solver for nonlinear MPC that exploits temporal decomposition so the network size stays independent of prediction horizon while still learning primal-dual updates toward KKT satisfaction.
engineering_relevance: It offers a faster, scalable alternative to conventional NMPC solvers for real-time control of large nonlinear systems, with comparable closed-loop performance and no observed constraint violations on the reported benchmark.
method: Learn primal-dual solver steps self-supervised, without precomputed optimal solutions.
Replace the monolithic horizon-dependent network with a temporally decomposed architecture.
Use closed-loop resampling to better match the training distribution to deployment behavior.
evidence_signal: On an economic NMPC benchmark of a CSTR cascade, the method scaled to larger problems than monolithic LISCO and achieved median speedups of up to 4× over IPOPT.
watch_item: The approach still depends on learned optimization dynamics, so robustness and generalization beyond the benchmarked closed-loop setting should be validated carefully.
paper_title: A Scalable Learned Iterative Solver for Nonlinear MPC via Temporal Decomposition
